## Findings
- claim-1: RWY work integrally in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) and prove that \(J_v\) is generated by two Schur-interval families; their proof uses Pieri identities and induction, not a stated Smith-form or unimodular-minor theorem. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 828-892]
- claim-2: St. Dizier–Yong define \(\overline{\Lambda}=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), with \(\overline{s}_\lambda\overline{s}_\mu=\sum_{\nu\subseteq(n-r)^r}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\nu}\overline{s}_\nu\), and prove lower-adjoined-family minimality using LR linear equations and coproduct reduction. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]
- claim-3: The stated St. Dizier–Yong algorithm is a terminating tensor reduction for valid \((n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\), not a theorem about integer Pieri presentation matrices, determinantal divisors, Smith diagonals, or complementary minors. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 494-516]
## Strategy
The provider record shows exactly `persisted:source-39,source-29,source-30`, yielding RWY (2011) and two renderings of St. Dizier–Yong (2024). It contains no query for Smith normal form, determinantal divisors, unimodular minors, or Pieri matrices. Thus the audit certificate is established: a provider search ran, but not the required targeted search.

For the current objects—integral degreewise Pieri presentation matrices for Schur intervals in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\)—the inspected RWY and St. Dizier–Yong passages supply generation/minimality or LR-tensor reductions, not Smith diagonals, determinantal divisors, or unimodular complementary minors. No determinant, unit, or finite matrix witness arises from this search audit.

## Gaps
The requested targeted external/arXiv literature search was not executed. Hence no bounded negative result for targeted Smith-form/Pieri-matrix literature is established. The comparison is bounded only to RWY (2011) and St. Dizier–Yong (2024).

## Next
Execute a distinct targeted search using combinations of “Smith normal form,” “determinantal divisors,” “unimodular minors,” “Pieri matrix,” “Schur functions,” and “Littlewood–Richardson,” then inspect and compare any full-text candidates under their exact matrix and coefficient-ring hypotheses.
